transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess… things have just gotten kind of hard to keep straight, especially at work. I work with a lot of tickets and receipts and notes, and customer jobs, and lately they all end up sort of piled together. I try to keep it organized, I really do, but then I look at it and I’m not sure what I’m supposed to handle first. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I don’t know if that’s the sort of thing you mean.
Have you noticed these kinds of difficulties with organization and focus for as long as you can remember, going back to childhood, or is this something that started more recently in your adult life?

I think it’s been there a long time, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I did try, but even in grade school my teachers would tell my mother I was bright, just… scattered. Like I’d talk out of turn, lose papers, need reminders to finish my work. So, no, I don’t think it just started recently.
Aside from the organization and focus difficulties, do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or find yourself acting or speaking impulsively without thinking things through?

I mean… yes, sometimes. I don’t think I’m trying to be rude or anything, but I’ll jump in with an answer before my daughter or a customer has even finished asking me something. Or like with a trainer at work, I’ll think I know where they’re going and answer too fast, and then I realize I answered the wrong thing. It’s embarrassing. I know I should wait.
Do you notice these same kinds of focus, organization, or impulsivity problems outside of work as well—like at home or in social situations—or are they mainly limited to your job?

It’s not only work, no. I mean, work is where it shows the most because there are customers and tickets and money involved, so mistakes are more obvious. We’ve had some late orders and a few billing mix-ups, and I know that’s caused some tense moments with coworkers and customers… which I feel terrible about.

At home and church it’s maybe not as dramatic, but it’s there. At church I used to help lead some planning things, and I’ve kind of stepped back from that because people were getting frustrated with me. I don’t want to be a problem for anyone, you know? So… yes, I guess it does happen outside of work too.
Have you been experiencing any ongoing feelings of sadness, worry, or anxiety recently that might be affecting your concentration?

I don’t think so… I mean, I worry some, like anybody would when work gets tense, but I wouldn’t say I’m walking around sad all the time or anything like that. At least, I don’t think that’s what’s causing it.

I guess I’m not totally sure what counts as “anxiety,” but this focus stuff feels like it’s been there even when I’m not especially upset. Does that make sense?
Do you currently use alcohol, recreational drugs, or any medications that might affect your concentration, or have you been told you have any medical conditions like thyroid problems or sleep apnea?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not using drugs or anything like that. I don’t really have anything I can think of that would explain it that way.

As far as medical stuff, nobody’s told me I have thyroid problems or sleep apnea. I’m not sure if there’s something else I should be thinking of, but nothing comes to mind.

Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days or more where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and had racing thoughts—different from your usual self?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m more irritated or keyed up, but not like… days where I’m euphoric or not needing sleep and feeling like a totally different person.

At least, nothing that stands out to me that way. Is that what you mean?

Do you often feel physically restless—like needing to get up and move around, tapping your foot, or fidgeting with your hands—even in situations where you're expected to sit still, such as during meetings or church?

I guess… yes, probably more than I’d like to admit. I try not to be disruptive, but during church committee meetings, or even those fabric-care trainings at work, I’ll catch myself needing to get up.

I’ll make it seem useful, like getting water, grabbing papers, or checking on something, but really I think I’m just having a hard time sitting there when everyone else seems fine. I don’t mean to be rude or anything. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?

Outside of situations where you're actually facing tasks or deadlines, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things—like health, finances, or family—that's hard to control, even when there's no immediate task at hand?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I worry like anybody does, I guess, about family or money here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s happening all the time when nothing’s going on.

It’s more when there’s something I’m supposed to be doing or I’m behind on something. If there isn’t some task or deadline hanging over me, I don’t think I’m just sitting around worrying about everything. Does that answer it okay?
